confirmedObservations: Both fans were rotating before the target change.
Both stored 1500 RPM targets and Battery Saver/manual state were retained.
Three consecutive paired zero tach readings followed; first paired zero was 10.755 seconds after the second target acknowledgement.
Exact original firmware targets/mode and installed intent were restored.
limitations: The 2000 RPM target was held only about 5.4 seconds before reduction.
There was no sustained unchanged-target control window.
There was no return-to-2000 phase to demonstrate resumed sustained rotation.
The original probe recorded CPU temperature but did not control GPU/workload activity.
Natural idle cooling or firmware behavior remains a possible explanation; the record does not establish that it was coincidence.

sequence: Hold 2000 RPM/manual unchanged for 30 seconds and verify sustained rotation.
Change only targets to 1500 RPM and observe mode, stored targets and tach for 30 seconds.
Return only targets to 2000 RPM and verify sustained rotation over 30 seconds.
Restore exact original firmware and software state.
proposedFollowup.stopRule: Stop all writes on ambiguous submission/readback; no retry or fallback.

interpretation: The observation is real, but the experiment did not isolate causation. Preserve historical records; withhold the consumer fan-stop capability rather than presenting an accepted target as proven forced fan stop.
